suggestions: This routine only researches and appends suggestions — it can't verify the cowork scheduler was tested or move this task to history for you. If you've confirmed the scheduler works, mark this complete yourself and it'll log to history automatically.

If “tested” means end-to-end (create/edit/complete/delete a task, toggle categories, public/private move), the recent commit history already shows a lot of that flow being exercised — categories, instant-complete with undo, and history-delete all landed recently.

Clickable links: run scratchpad/notes text through a URL-matching regex (e.g. /(https?://[^s]+)/g) at render time and wrap matches in <a href=... target="_blank" rel="noopener"> — no schema change needed, just a render-layer fix.

Per-note subtasks: add a small array field (e.g. task.noteItems: [{id, text, done, created}]) alongside the existing free-text scratchpad, rendered as its own checkbox list — keeps the current scratchpad intact for freeform notes while giving completable sub-items.

Multiple notes: if you want notes to behave like suggestions (their own list, individually editable/removable), model them the same way — an array of {id, text, updated} objects instead of one big scratchpad string — so each note can be clicked and edited in isolation rather than reopening one large textbox.

please implement: On the dropdown/popup/sidebar question: recommend reusing the same inline expand pattern already built for History entries (the ▸/▾ toggle) rather than a new sidebar or popup. Click a task card (or a small chevron) to expand a details panel in place showing notes + suggestions, no navigation away. Reasons: (1) it is already built and proven in historyNodeEl/historyNodeDetailHtml, so it is mostly copy-adapt, not new UX; (2) it works the same on mobile and desktop with no extra responsive layout to design, unlike a sidebar; (3) a popup/modal interrupts the flow of scanning a list, an inline expand does not.

Only appears on tasks that actually have any of that; editing still happens via double-click (title) or the Assistance tab (notes/checkboxes). This keeps notes visible even after turning assist off.

suggestions: On the dropdown/popup/sidebar question: recommend reusing the same inline expand pattern already built for History entries (the ▸/▾ toggle) rather than a new sidebar or popup. Click a task card (or a small chevron) to expand a details panel in place showing notes + suggestions, no navigation away. Reasons: (1) it is already built and proven in historyNodeEl/historyNodeDetailHtml, so it is mostly copy-adapt, not new UX; (2) it works the same on mobile and desktop with no extra responsive layout to design, unlike a sidebar; (3) a popup/modal interrupts the flow of scanning a list, an inline expand does not.

Concrete approach: give every active task-card the same expand/collapse affordance as history nodes — a chevron button, an `expandedTaskNodes` Set keyed by taskKey(task), and a detail block rendered under the title showing noteItems (read-only ✓/plain list, since editing already happens via double-click and the Assistance tab) plus suggestions if any. Only show the chevron when the task actually has notes or suggestions, same as `hasDetail` does for history.

⚠ Heads-up: while implementing this I found a real bug worth fixing — the site loads task data once into memory and every save (add/edit/delete a note) rewrites the whole tasks.json from that in-memory snapshot instead of refetching first. If two edits happen close together (e.g. a stale tab + a fresh one, or you and an automated routine), the second write can silently clobber the first — which is exactly what just happened to my note on this task. A fix would be to refetch the file's current sha/content right before each write and merge, or at least warn when the sha on disk has moved since load.
